JSON: Name: lctfound_diffusion_pretraining Title: Diffusion-pretrained vision foundation model for multi-task lung CT imaging including diagnosis, pixel-level enhancement, and 3D surgical modeling Short Hypothesis: Pretraining a U-net DDPM diffusion model on a large, multi-center lung CT dataset with joint encoding of imaging and basic clinical metadata produces feature representations that, when fine-tuned, yield statistically significant improvements in low-incidence disease diagnosis, low-dose CT enhancement, sparse-view CT reconstruction, and whole-lung 3D segmentation compared to standard self-supervised pretraining methods. Related Work: Prior approaches for lung CT and medical imaging foundation models fall into two classes: contrastive/encoder-only self-supervised methods and generative adversarial / task-specific reconstruction methods. Contrastive and masked-image-pretraining methods produce strong global semantic features but have limited pixel-level generative fidelity and struggle to restore fine vascular and airway detail. GAN-based image-to-image methods achieve high perceptual quality for denoising or modality translation but suffer from instability, mode collapse, and limited few-shot generalization. Existing medical foundation efforts either focus on 2D radiology modalities with small task scopes or use 3D transfer in narrow domains; they commonly lack (1) very large, multi-center lung-CT pretraining corpora, (2) conditioning on basic clinical imaging metadata, (3) a unified model able to support both pixel-level synthesis and diagnostic-level prediction, and (4) systematic evaluation on few-shot, low-incidence tasks and cross-center generalization. Abstract: We propose a diffusion-based self-supervised vision foundation approach for lung CT imaging that targets both pixel-level image synthesis and diagnostic-level prediction. The method pretrains a U-net architecture augmented with cross-attention transformer blocks using a denoising diffusion probabilistic model on a large, multi-center lung CT corpus and jointly encodes basic imaging metadata as conditional inputs. The pre-trained model is adapted to multiple downstream tasks—low-dose CT enhancement, sparse-view reconstruction, virtual CT angiography synthesis, low-incidence lesion segmentation, NSCLC prognosis and neoadjuvant response prediction, and whole-lung 3D anatomical modeling—via lightweight adapters or full fine-tuning. The main contribution is a single foundation model that unifies high-fidelity pixel generation with clinically relevant representation learning to improve few-shot performance and cross-center robustness. Expected outcomes include improved image quality metrics for reconstruction and denoising, higher diagnostic accuracy and segmentation Dice on low-incidence diseases, and more reliable 3D anatomical models for surgical navigation. Experiments: Datasets: Pretraining dataset: LungCT-28M (105,184 CT scans; multi-center). Downstream datasets: mediastinal neoplasm segmentation (standardized pixel-level annotations from 7 centers; split into train/val/test and external centers), NSCLC prognosis (LUNG1, N≈420 scans with survival labels; internal split train/val/test), PAP classification (270 positive cases + matched negatives from Guangzhou cohort; internal/external splits), virtual CTA paired dataset (102 patients; train=17 pairs, test=85 pairs), sparse-view reconstruction dataset (9 training scans, 1 held-out test scan; generated 8/16/32 projection simulations), low-dose enhancement dataset (Mayo2016 matched low/high dose pairs; train/test splits), whole-lung 3D segmentation dataset (35 CT scans with 21-structure ground truth; train/val/test). Baselines: MAE pretraining, MedSAM, Med3D/RadImageNet, InternImage, Swin3D, UNet trained from scratch, GAN-based enhancers (WGAN/DualGAN), CTA-GAN, Pixel2Pixel, CondDDPM, DuDoTrans, DIF-Gaussian, SAX-NeRF, nnU-Net for segmentation. Evaluation metrics: classification AUROC and AUPRC, Dice and IoU for segmentation, PSNR/SSIM/VIF/RMSE/LPIPS/CLIPIQA for pixel tasks, Kaplan–Meier survival curves and log-rank p-values for prognosis stratification, computational cost (FLOPs, inference latency), and statistical significance via bootstrap (1000 iterations) and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Experimental setup: pretrain DDPM U-net on LungCT-28M for N epochs with specified scheduler; compare two transfer modes per downstream task: linear-probe on frozen encoder vs full fine-tuning; evaluate across internal and external center test sets. Ablations: (1) remove clinical metadata conditioning, (2) replace cross-attention blocks with standard convolutional blocks, (3) pretrain on 50% vs 100% pretraining data, (4) swap diffusion pretraining for MAE pretraining keeping same backbone, (5) freeze encoder vs fine-tune decoder-only, (6) few-shot regimes (1%, 5%, 10% of training data) for low-incidence tasks. Comparisons: measure absolute and relative improvements of primary metrics over each baseline and report significance. Risk Factors and Limitations: Technical failure modes: model may overfit scanner- or center-specific imaging protocols producing poor cross-vendor generalization; diffusion pretraining may fail to capture consistent 3D z-axis continuity when trained predominantly on 2D slices. Data and evaluation biases: pretraining and downstream labels reflect available clinical populations and may under-represent rare demographics, causing biased performance; NLP-extracted labels from reports may contain systematic errors. Scalability and compute: DDPM pretraining at scale requires large GPU clusters and prolonged wall-time; inference latency and memory footprint may be unsuitable for real-time intraoperative use. Generative risks: synthesized vascular or lesion detail (virtual CTA, super-resolution) can hallucinate clinically misleading structures. Generalization limits: improvements on held-out centers may not translate to all geographic regions or scanner types; few-shot gains for extremely rare conditions may remain insufficient for clinical adoption. Regulatory and validation constraints: diagnostic and interventional use require prospective clinical validation and regulatory clearance not covered by retrospective experiments.
